items.title: OPEN: A Benchmark Dataset and Baseline for Older Adult Patient Engagement Recognition in Virtual Rehabilitation Learning Environments
items.abstract: Engagement in virtual learning is critical to participant satisfaction, performance, and adherence, particularly in domains such as online education and virtual rehabilitation, where interactive communication is essential for success. However, accurately measuring engagement in virtual group settings remains a significant challenge. There is growing interest in leveraging artificial intelligence for large-scale, real-world, and automated engagement recognition. Although engagement has been widely studied among younger populations in academic contexts, research methods and datasets focused on older adults in virtual and telehealth learning environments remain limited. Existing approaches often overlook the contextual relevance of learning materials and the longitudinal dynamics of engagement across sessions. This paper presents OPEN (Older adult Patient ENgagement), a novel dataset created to support the development of artificial intelligence models for engagement recognition. The dataset was collected from eleven older adults participating in virtual group learning sessions over six weeks as part of their cardiac rehabilitation programs, yielding over 35 hours of data, which represents the largest dataset of its kind. While raw video is withheld to protect privacy, the publicly released data include facial, hand, and body joint landmarks, as well as behavioral and affective features extracted from video. Observational annotations comprise second-level binary engagement states, emotional and behavioral labels, and context-type details, such as whether the instructor addressed the group or an individual. Multiple versions of the dataset were generated using sample lengths of 5, 10, and 30 seconds, as well as variable-length segments. To demonstrate its utility, various machine learning and deep learning models were trained on the annotated data, achieving engagement recognition accuracy as high as 81%. OPEN provides a scalable foundation not only for advancing personalized, artificial intelligence-driven engagement recognition in aging populations but also for contributing to broader engagement recognition research.

items.title: Operational drivers of fuel performance in Ro–Ro shipping
items.abstract: This study investigates operational drivers of fuel performance in maritime transport using 22 months of high-resolution sensor data from two Ro-Ro sister vessels. A hybrid benchmark model is developed to derive a speed-and draught-independent performance indicator, enabling consistent evaluation of efficiency and environmental impact. Results show that fuel performance is primarily governed by physical operating conditions, while hull condition and human factors are associated with variability in observed performance. Hull degradation leads to efficiency losses through increased resistance and associated operational responses, with implications for fuel consumption and emissions. Variability related to captains and crews are explained by how operating conditions are selected and managed rather than by intrinsic performance differences. A machine learning-based decision support pilot showed a 1.9 percentage-point improvement in fuel performance and reduced variability across operators. Overall, the findings demonstrate how maintenance, operational decisions, and data-driven tools can enhance transport efficiency and support maritime decarbonisation.

items.title: Overweight and obesity as predictors of work-related upper extremity disability among dentists in Arak, Iran: a cross-sectional study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs) pose a significant occupational health challenge for dental professionals due to prolonged static postures and repetitive movements. While obesity is a known risk factor for MSDs, its specific association with upper extremity disability among dentists remains underexplored.To investigate the association between body mass index (BMI) and work-related upper extremity disability among dentists in Arak, Iran. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among 276 dentists recruited from dental offices and clinics in Arak using convenience sampling. Data were collected using a demographic and occupational questionnaire, the Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire (NMQ), and the Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand (DASH) questionnaire. BMI was categorized according to World Health Organization criteria. Binary logistic regression and chi-square (χ²) tests were employed to determine factors associated with upper extremity disability. Statistical significance was defined as a p-value < 0.05. Results The prevalence of overweight and obesity was 36.6% and 19.2%, respectively. The shoulder was the most frequently affected site (58.7%), followed by the wrist/hand (53.6%) and neck (47.8%). After adjusting for gender, age, and work experience, overweight (adjusted OR = 1.84, 95% CI: 1.02–3.32, p = 0.04) and obesity (adjusted OR = 2.98, 95% CI: 1.42–6.25, p = 0.004) were significantly associated with higher odds of upper extremity disability compared to normal-weight dentists. No significant associations were observed for gender, age, or work experience. Conclusion Elevated BMI is independently associated with upper extremity disability among dentists in a dose-response manner. These findings highlight the need for integrated weight management and ergonomic interventions in occupational health strategies for dental professionals to reduce MSD burden.

items.title: Parameter-Efficient Multi-Task Fine-Tuning in Code-Related Tasks
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have proven highly effective in automating software engineering tasks, bridging natural language and code semantics to achieve notable results in code generation and summarization. However, their scale incurs substantial computational costs, making full fine-tuning impractical. Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) methods like QLoRA enable efficient specialization with lower resource demands. Recent studies show QLoRA-optimized Large Code Models (LCMs) perform strongly across diverse tasks, yet it remains unclear whether this effectiveness persists when a single model is QLoRA fine-tuned for multiple code-related tasks. The interaction between Multi-task fine-tuning and QLoRA optimization, and how transfer learning affects correctness and quality of generated artifacts, remains largely unexplored. We investigate Multi-task QLoRA fine-tuning — a representative parameter-efficient method from the LoRA family — across three representative tasks: code generation, translation, and summarization. We evaluate functional correctness through execution-based and similarity-based metrics, complemented by comprehensive code quality analysis–an aspect largely overlooked in prior work. Our findings show that Multi-task QLoRA effectively leverages transfer learning, achieving competitive or superior performance at the 1.5B, 3B, and 7B configurations relative to both Single-task QLoRA and Multi-task full fine-tuning. Larger models demonstrate more consistent balance between correctness and quality, whereas smaller models preserve functionality but exhibit a higher incidence of quality-related issues.

items.title: Pathways for Teaching Model Reform Driven by the Interaction between New Quality Productive Forces and Vocational Education: The Case of Electrical Automation Technology
items.abstract: Electrical automation teaching must prepare students to commission interconnected equipment, diagnose faults and judge technical changes against operating requirements. These tasks bring the relationship between new quality productive forces and vocational education into the classroom: industrial change reshapes competence requirements, while skilled graduates and college technical services can support the adoption and improvement of production technologies. This paper develops a teaching reform proposal for the three-year higher vocational Electrical Automation Technology programme. It combines policy and document analysis, conceptual comparison and instructional design, using the national professional teaching standard and research on project-based learning, workplace learning and authentic assessment. The analysis identifies coordination problems involving curriculum sequencing, practical training, enterprise participation, assessment and resource provision. A proposed project, upgrading a conveying and sorting cell while examining its energy use, connects programmable logic controller programming, variable-frequency drives, human-machine interfaces and industrial networking. Students move from requirement analysis and simulation to supervised commissioning, fault diagnosis and evidence-based review. Assessment combines project documentation and operating records with individual explanation and transfer tasks. The proposed reciprocal mechanism depends on translating workplace requirements into assessable learning tasks and returning reviewed teaching outcomes to enterprise discussion, staff training or technical service. These routes require sustained teacher coordination and explicit responsibility for accepting changes. The paper presents a design for subsequent piloting; it reports no institutional intervention or measured learning gains. A future evaluation should examine competence transfer separately from any claim about enterprise productivity, because a functioning classroom prototype provides insufficient evidence of industrial impact.

items.title: Pemeriksaan HBsAG Menggunakan Metode Imunokromatografi Pada Pemulung di TPA Sekitar Lowok Waru Kota Malang
items.abstract: Waste pickers are among the occupational groups potentially exposed to biological hazards, including the hepatitis B virus (HBV), due to contact with waste materials and sharp objects in their working environment. This study aimed to describe the results of Hepatitis B Surface Antigen (HBsAg) screening among waste pickers at three waste disposal sites in Malang City. A quantitative descriptive approach was employed involving 15 male waste pickers from Candi Panggung, Tlogomas, and Merjosari waste disposal sites, selected through purposive sampling. HBsAg screening was performed using capillary blood specimens with the immunochromatographic rapid test (ICT) method. The collected data were analyzed descriptively using frequency distributions and percentages. The results showed that the largest proportion of respondents was aged 40–50 years (33%), and all respondents (100%) had worked as waste pickers for more than five years. HBsAg screening identified 12 respondents (80%) with non-reactive results and 3 respondents (20%) with reactive results. These findings indicate the presence of reactive HBsAg screening results among the participants; however, further laboratory examinations are required to confirm their hepatitis B infection status. Due to the limited sample size and descriptive research design, the findings cannot establish the source of infection or a causal relationship between occupational exposure and HBV transmission. This study highlights the importance of occupational health education, appropriate personal protective equipment, and access to follow-up healthcare services for waste pickers.

items.abstract: Breast cancer control in Indonesia is a government priority under the National Cancer Control Strategy 2024–2034, yet early prevention education has not equally reached adolescents with autism spectrum disorder and multiple disabilities. Rumah Autis recognizes this risk but faces limited understanding and a lack of inclusive breast self-examination (SADARI) educational media. Existing media mostly rely on lengthy texts, abstract verbal explanations, or sensory-unfriendly demonstrations, whereas adolescents with special needs require repeatable and easy-to-imitate visual information. Therefore, a program was conducted to develop and train 50 participants—comprising parents, volunteers, and the Rumah Autis caregiver team—on using artificial intelligence (AI)-based demonstration videos and pictogram cards called SADARI Ceria (Breast Self-Examination: Smart, Friendly, and Inclusive). items.title: PENGEMBANGAN COURSE TERINTEGRASI AI BERBASIS PROBLEM BASED LEARNING UNTUK MENINGKATKAN KEMAMPUAN PENERAPAN PROSEDUR DAN PEMECAHAN MASALAH SISWA SMP
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Informatics education requires instructional designs that connect conceptual understanding with procedural application and contextual problem-solving. This study aimed to develop an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-integrated course based on Problem-Based Learning (PBL) to support these two competencies among junior high school students. The product was developed using the Moodle platform by combining digital learning materials, problem-based activities, and AI support in the form of explanations and learning-material summaries. The needs analysis involved 113 students, while the learning-outcome evaluation employed an experimental group and a control group, each consisting of 34 students, using pretests and posttests. The needs analysis revealed percentages of 23% for decomposition, 50% for pattern recognition, 35% for abstraction, and 44% for algorithms. In procedural application of computational thinking, the experimental group's mean score increased from 58.40 to 82.60, whereas the control group's mean score increased from 57.90 to 70.30. For contextual problem-solving, the experimental group's mean score increased from 56.80 to 83.10, while the control group's mean score rose from 57.20 to 71.40. Descriptively, the experimental group demonstrated greater improvement in both measured competencies. These findings indicate the potential of the developed AI-integrated PBL course to support Informatics learning; however, its statistical effectiveness must be confirmed through inferential testing. items.title: Perceived AI literacy and TPACK in pre-service teacher education: mediating roles of perceived usefulness, ease of use, and value in blended learning
items.abstract: Background The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into blended learning requires pre-service teachers to develop AI-related competencies and the ability to integrate technology into pedagogy. This study examines how perceived AI literacy and technological pedagogical content knowledge (TPACK) are associated with deep learning through perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and perceived value of AI use. Methods A cross-sectional survey was completed by 423 pre-service teachers enrolled in blended learning courses at a university in China. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM), with covariance-based structural equation modeling and fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA) used as complementary robustness and configurational analyses. Results Perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, and perceived value of AI use significantly mediated the relationships between the two competencies and deep learning. All six indirect pathways were significant in both the PLS-SEM and covariance-based SEM analyses. The fsQCA revealed an equifinal and asymmetric structure: multiple, partly substitutable conditions were sufficient for high deep learning, and no single condition was necessary for either high or low deep learning. Conclusions The findings integrate the technology acceptance model and expectancy-value theory to explain how pre-service teachers' competencies and perceptions relate to deep learning in AI-enhanced blended environments. Teacher education should support technical competence alongside positive perceptions of AI's utility, usability, and value. Because the measures were self-reported and collected cross-sectionally at one university, the findings are interpreted as associational and configurational rather than causal.
